passage: Note for the home-science file, Thursday. Tanvir cooked onion pakoras for the class demonstration today. Before touching anything he washed his hands with soap and tied back his sleeves. He used one board for the raw onions and a clean plate for the fried pakoras, never mixing them. When the oil was heating he stood at the stove with his eyes on the pan and turned the handle inward. He did not leave the stove, even when a friend called him. He switched off the gas himself and let the oil cool before it went anywhere. I have asked him to help two classmates with their stove habits next week. Darshan, teacher

qa.q: Which food did Tanvir cook for the demonstration?
qa.a: Tanvir cooked onion pakoras for the class demonstration.

qa.q: What was Tanvir probably feeling when a friend called him and he stayed at the stove?
qa.a: He was probably focused and a little proud of his responsibility, choosing to stay with the hot oil instead of being distracted.

qa.q: What did Tanvir do to keep raw and cooked food apart?
qa.a: He used one board for the raw onions and a clean plate for the fried pakoras, never mixing them.

qa.q: How might Darshan see Tanvir's stove habits?
qa.a: Darshan sees careful habits that prevent burns and stomach trouble, which is why Tanvir is asked to help two classmates next week.

grounding: Shows a young cook washing hands, keeping raw and cooked food apart, watching hot oil and staying at the stove.

passage: Saturday. First time alone in the kitchen, Amma was out at a wedding. I made egg curry for my cousin Saurabh and me. I washed my hands, then washed them again after cracking the eggs. The knife for the onions and the raw-egg bowl went into the sink, and the salad got a fresh board. When the oil got hot, Saurabh begged me to let him try tadka. I said no, and turned the pan handle towards the wall. The gas stayed on the whole time and so did I. Not once did I go to the door. It felt a bit boring. Nothing burnt and nobody got a sore stomach. Chetan

qa.q: Who did Chetan make egg curry for?
qa.a: Chetan made egg curry for Saurabh and Chetan.

qa.q: What did Chetan feel when Saurabh begged to try the tadka?
qa.a: Chetan felt protective and firm, saying no and turning the pan handle to the wall, even though being so careful felt a bit boring.

qa.q: What safe habits did Chetan keep while the gas was on?
qa.a: Chetan stayed at the stove, kept the handle turned to the wall and never went to the door.

qa.q: How might Saurabh have felt when Chetan said no to the tadka?
qa.a: Saurabh was probably disappointed but safe, since hot oil is not something to try without care.

grounding: Shows a young cook washing hands, separating raw and cooked things, watching hot oil and never leaving the stove.

passage: In the village near Namchi, Tenzin, fifteen, was cooking dinner for the first time while his mother was at the monastery. His cousin Ankita watched from the doorway. Before touching anything, Tenzin washed his hands with soap at the tap outside. He cut the raw chicken on one board and the vegetables on another, then washed the knife. When the oil in the wok began to shimmer, he lowered the chicken in slowly, away from himself. Ankita's phone rang; she handed it to him. "Aunty wants you." Tenzin turned the gas off first, then took the call. "Why'd you switch it off?" Ankita asked. "Amma says the stove never stays alone. Not even for a minute."

qa.q: Where was Tenzin's mother?
qa.a: At the monastery.

qa.q: How might Tenzin have felt cooking dinner alone for the first time?
qa.a: He probably felt a little nervous but careful and responsible, following each safe habit.

qa.q: Which of Tenzin's habits made his cooking safe?
qa.a: Washing his hands, using separate boards for raw chicken and vegetables, lowering food into hot oil carefully and turning off the gas before taking the call.

qa.q: How does Ankita see Tenzin switching off the gas?
qa.a: Ankita is puzzled at first, not seeing why he would turn it off for a short call.

grounding: Shows a young cook washing hands, keeping raw food apart, watching hot oil and never leaving the stove untended.

passage: Ingrid, sixteen, was making dinner for her family in Stockholm while her parents worked late. Her friend Marek had come over to help. He reached for the salad bowl right after handling the raw fish. "Wait," Ingrid said. "Wash first. And use the other board for the cucumber." He rolled his eyes but did it. When the pan of potatoes started spitting oil, she turned down the heat and stood back, not leaving the kitchen. Marek wanted to show her a video in the living room. "After," she said, "when the stove's off." Dinner was a little late. But no one got a burn, and no one was ill the next day.

qa.q: What did Marek reach for right after handling the raw fish?
qa.a: He reached for the salad bowl.

qa.q: How did Marek feel about Ingrid's instructions?
qa.a: He felt a little annoyed and impatient, rolling his eyes, but followed them.

qa.q: Which habits kept the kitchen safe?
qa.a: Washing after touching raw fish, using a separate board, turning down spitting oil and never leaving the stove to watch a video.

qa.q: How might Ingrid's parents feel coming home to dinner?
qa.a: They would likely feel relieved and proud that Ingrid cooked safely, even if dinner was a little late.

grounding: Shows a teenager cooking with safe habits: hand washing, separate boards, watching hot oil and not leaving the stove.

passage: The school cookery club met on Saturday mornings in the home-science lab, and this week Damini and Shreya were making chicken fried rice. Damini washed her hands with soap before touching anything, then took the red chopping board for the raw chicken and the green one for the vegetables. "Why two boards?" Shreya asked. "Raw chicken juice on the cucumber is how people end up sick," Damini said, and washed the red board and knife in hot soapy water as soon as she was done. She patted the vegetables dry before they went into the oil so it wouldn't spit, and turned the wok handle inwards. When Shreya called from the next counter, "Come look, my rice is stuck!", Damini switched off the gas first, then went. Ms Kapoor, walking past, nodded and moved on to the next table without a word.

qa.q: Which chopping board did Damini use for the raw chicken?
qa.a: The red chopping board.

qa.q: How does Damini seem to feel while she cooks?
qa.a: Damini seems calm and confident, moving through each safe habit without fuss or worry.

qa.q: Which of Damini's habits prevents a burn or fire, and why?
qa.a: Switching off the gas before leaving the stove, drying vegetables before the oil and turning the handle inwards all stop the pan from spitting, catching or being knocked.

qa.q: What might Ms Kapoor's nod and silence suggest about how she sees Damini?
qa.a: Ms Kapoor seems to trust Damini's habits, feeling no need to step in or remind her of anything.

grounding: Illustrates a young cook who washes hands, keeps raw and cooked food apart, handles hot oil carefully and never leaves the lit stove.
